q6.answer: The status lives on the report_exports record in the primary database, which holds status, attempt, last error, completed_at and related fields. The page learns of changes by polling GET /api/reports/{id}/exports/latest every 5 seconds while the export is queued or running, and it calls that same endpoint on every page load, so reopening the page later shows the current state.

q7.answer: The job never loads the whole report. It reads keyset pages of 5,000 rows (row_id greater than last_row_id, LIMIT 5000) from the read replica, encodes each page to CSV bytes, and appends them to an in-memory part buffer. When the buffer reaches 8 MB it is uploaded as one multipart part, so peak report data held is about 12 MB, well under the 512 MB worker limit.

q8.answer: Parts already uploaded stay in the open multipart upload, and the checkpoint on the export record keeps the upload_id, the list of part_number and etag pairs, and last_row_id. The unuploaded in-memory buffer is lost. The next attempt, after 60 or 300 seconds, resumes from last_row_id under the same upload, re-derives the same part number and rows, and replaces any partial part. Nothing is visible at the object key until complete_multipart succeeds, so no partial file can be downloaded.

q9.answer: They are captured on the report_exports record at the click (step 3b), when the record is inserted with the filters and columns from the request. The job payload carries only the export_id, and the job reads the filters and columns from that record when it runs.

q10.answer: A partial unique index on report_exports over (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running enforces it in the database. The second insert is rejected, and that request reads the active record and returns it, so no second job starts.

q11.answer: The file must already be complete: complete_multipart has succeeded and the record has been set to done with completed_at and the object key (step 9), and then send_email runs (step 10). If the queue reruns the job after the export is done and email_sent_at is set, it returns at once. If it is done but email_sent_at is empty, it sends only the email and does not rebuild the file.

q12.answer: A small export keeps nothing, so there is no retry or saved state. A failure before the first byte returns 503. A failure mid-stream, or the 50-second or 10,000-row guard, makes the server abort the connection, so the browser reports a failed download rather than a short file, and the page says Try again later.
